=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Package

The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" asks us to ignore everything marked [STANDARD] because both sides have supposedly cleared it. That is the Seller's characterisation, not something we have agreed, so I have reviewed the whole package. Nothing in the Seller's documents is cleared until Wattlebridge signs off.

## Core problem

The Seller's package moves nearly all known risk onto the Buyer, through a combination of general disclosure, a buyer-knowledge bar, and a low cap. Every known issue in the Disclosure Letter is disclosed against the warranties. Once disclosed, it is effectively unrecoverable as a warranty claim. So known problems must be fixed through price, debt-like deductions, conditions, or specific indemnities. They cannot be left to the warranty regime.

## Known exposures

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Seller position | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 | Release "following Completion" | Debt should be repaid from proceeds at Completion on a debt-free basis |
| Employee bonuses (DD-005) | 420,000 + on-costs | Not in funds flow | Transaction-triggered debt-like item; payroll tax and super not addressed |
| Ironquay SOW3 (DD-010) | 180,000 open | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | IP transfer conditional on payment; no assignment in data room |
| Sandbar renewals | 330,000 | "Ordinary course" | Unverified; terms and termination rights unknown |
| Privacy incident (DD-006) | Unquantified | "Not expected to be material" | Possible notifiable data breach; scope unknown |
| **Subtotal (quantified)** | **~4,130,000** | | Before on-costs and before the unquantified privacy exposure |

The Seller's general cap of AUD 4.8m would be largely absorbed by these items if they were claimable. Because they are disclosed, the cap and the warranty regime give the Buyer little protection against them.

## Issues by clause

**1. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (DL 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).** This is the most serious issue. It deems the Buyer to have been told everything in the data room, which is effectively a blanket disclosure against all warranties. Push back: delete it. Disclosure should be specific, fair, and reasonably particularised against each warranty. Data room documents should not be deemed disclosed.

**2. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3).** The Buyer loses any claim for anything its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room. This is a sandbagging exclusion. Push back: delete it, and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause so the Buyer's knowledge does not reduce its rights. Known matters should instead be dealt with through price and specific indemnities.

**3. General liability cap (cl 12.1).** AUD 4.8m is 20% of price. That is low for a deal with this disclosure profile. Push for a higher general cap (for example 30–50%, to be tested against Buyer's valuation model) and separate, higher caps or uncapped liability (up to purchase price) for title, capacity, tax and fundamental warranties.

**4. Thresholds (cl 12.2).** The AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k excess-only basket mean the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of losses. Push for a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar), a lower de minimis, and aggregation of related claims (for example the three Sandbar renewals or related privacy losses) so they are not individually excluded.

**5. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13).** The 18-month general period is too short for matters like Ironquay IP ownership, privacy claims and tax. The clause that applies any limitation to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" would also pull title and capacity claims into the 18-month window. Push for:
- General warranties: at least 3 years, or longer for IP and privacy.
- Title, capacity and fundamental warranties: the statutory limitation period, which in NSW is generally 6 years for contract claims and longer if the SPA is executed as a deed. Confirm with NSW counsel.
- Tax: survival until the relevant ATO assessment periods have closed, plus a buffer.

**6. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).** This would catch fraud and possibly equitable remedies. Push for carve-outs for fraud, specific indemnities, title and capacity, and equitable relief. Non-reliance should not protect fraudulent misrepresentation.

**7. Title and capacity subject to general caps (Fundamental / Title).** Title should not be treated as administratively equivalent to general warranties. Push back: title and capacity sit outside the general cap and time limits, up to the purchase price. The Seller's reliance on the share register (DD-012) is not verification. Require ASIC company extracts, a PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no encumbrances, and registered transfer documents at Completion.

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL 2).** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (roughly AUD 3.6m, implying around AUD 12m total FY26 revenue, to be checked). The Seller proposes to treat consent as "satisfied" on delivery of written consent, but DL 2 confirms no final consent exists and the conditions in cl 11.3 are unsatisfied. Push back:
- Final written consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, must be a condition precedent.
- The Seller should bear all consent costs and fees.
- Replace "reasonable endeavours" with "best endeavours" on the Seller's side.
- Include a long-stop date and a Buyer right to terminate or re-price if consent is not obtained.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL 3).** A release "following Completion" means the Buyer could inherit a AUD 3.2m secured facility with no discharge. On a debt-free basis, the facility should be repaid from proceeds at Completion. Push for:
- A payoff letter.
- Discharge of security and PPSR deregistration delivered at Completion.
- An indemnity for any residual liability.
- Verification that the AUD 3.2m is actually deducted in the price mechanics. The funds flow is described as reflecting "agreed price mechanics", which is not sufficient.

**10. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4).** A limitation to the SOW3 payment is inadequate. The Buyer needs:
- Payment of the AUD 180k before Completion by the Seller, or a debt-like deduction.
- A confirmatory assignment of Project Materials as a Completion deliverable.
- A full IP ownership and chain-of-title indemnity, including third-party claims and remediation costs.
- A warranty that all contractor IP has been validly assigned.

**11. Employee bonuses (DL 5).** The AUD 420k in conditional Completion bonuses is transaction-related and should be a Seller cost or a debt-like deduction. Employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax and superannuation guarantee, currently 12%) are not addressed and should be covered by the Seller. Confirm the bonuses do not depend on Buyer-side decisions.

**12. Privacy and export incident (DD-006; DL 6; Schedule 6 / cl 4.6).** The Seller calls this preliminary, but the data includes names, emails, roles and activity timestamps, and the export went to an unintended external address. Given revenue of roughly AUD 12m, the Privacy Act's small business exemption is unlikely to apply. The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme may be triggered if the incident is an eligible data breach, so the Buyer needs a view on this quickly. Push for:
- A forensic investigation before Completion, at the Seller's cost.
- A specific, uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity for losses from the incident.
- A privacy compliance warranty.
- Seller responsibility for any notifications required for pre-Completion events, with Buyer control after Completion.
- A retention or escrow to secure the indemnity.

**13. Office lease (DL 7).** The lease has a notification obligation and may require landlord consent to the share sale. Push for confirmation, and for landlord consent or waiver as a condition if required.

**14. Supplier renewals (cl ~4; DL 8).** The three Sandbar renewals total AUD 330k and are related. Read together, they look like a single commitment. Push for:
- Full copies of the contracts and confirmation of term, termination rights, and pricing.
- Treatment as debt-like items if they are not in the ordinary course or are above market.
- Aggregation for basket purposes.

**15. Mossvale (DL 9).** Confirm that the change-of-control provisions are not triggered by the share sale. "Restriction on assignment" may not cover a share sale, but the clause must be read in full.

**16. Tax and IP (general regime).** The Seller considers these settled. They are not. Push for a specific pre-Completion tax indemnity (not subject to the basket or de minimis, and capped at price), with survival until the relevant assessment periods have closed. IP warranties should cover chain of title, contractor assignments and open-source use.

**17. Reservation of rights (DL 1.4, 11).** These are standard and acceptable, but they do not change the analysis above.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "efficiency" framing.** All clauses remain open. Do not accept [STANDARD] labels as cleared.
2. **Delete general disclosure** of the data room and public registers. Require specific, particularised disclosure only.
3. **Delete the buyer-knowledge bar** (cl 8.3) and add a pro-sandbagging clause.
4. **Increase the general cap** and set title, capacity, fundamental and tax warranties at up to purchase price, outside the general cap and time limits.
5. **Replace the excess-only basket** with a tipping basket and lower de minimis, with aggregation of related claims.
6. **Extend time limits** for general warranties, with statutory-period protection for title and capacity, and tax survival until the relevant assessment periods close.
7. **Carve out fraud, specific indemnities and equitable remedies** from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses.
8. **Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent**, with a long-stop date and Buyer termination or re-pricing rights.
9. **Repay Riverlark at Completion** from proceeds, with discharge of security delivered at Completion. Verify the price deduction.
10. **Require the Seller to fix Ironquay IP** before Completion: pay the AUD 180k, deliver a confirmatory assignment, and provide a full IP indemnity.
11. **Treat the AUD 420k bonuses and on-costs** as Seller costs or debt-like deductions, and include them in the funds flow.
12. **Require a privacy forensic review** before Completion, with a specific indemnity and a retention or escrow. Assess notification obligations urgently.
13. **Verify title independently** (ASIC extracts, PPSR search, transfer documents) and do not rely on the Seller's register.
14. **Resolve lease consent, Sandbar terms and Mossvale change-of-control** before signing.

**Caveat:** This is a commercial and legal issues review to help the deal team prioritise, not formal advice. Specific points, including the NSW limitation periods, payroll tax and super rates, Privacy Act notification analysis, stamp duty and sandbagging position, should be confirmed with NSW counsel and tax advisers before they are relied on in negotiation.
